headline: NEW to scans (UN Geneva briefing Fri Oct 23) -- Taiz City 20 days cut off by Ansar Allah siege
dek: Taiz City has been encircled by Ansar Allah forces for 20 days and counting: access roads cut, very little fuel, food or supplies reaching the city since. WFP: more than 800,000 people in Taiz cut off from assistance, including 600,000 who depend on humanitarian assistance and 200,000 women and…
sources: UN OCHA spokesman Jens Laerke and WFP Regional Communications Officer Azfar Deen, Geneva briefing Oct 23; WFP Yemen statement Oct 14 (800,000 figure)
fault_line: 20 days cut off: is Taiz a siege tactic in a civil war — or a city being starved while the region watches the Gulf?

sections.what_happened: Taiz City has been encircled by Ansar Allah forces for 20 days and counting: access roads cut, very little fuel, food or supplies reaching the city since. WFP: more than 800,000 people in Taiz cut off from assistance, including 600,000 who depend on humanitarian assistance and 200,000 women and children; wheat flour stocks nearly exhausted. OCHA: water production in the city fallen by about half because trucked water depends on scarce diesel; truck-water cost roughly tripled. UN: ~260,000 displaced in Taiz/Lahij since August escalation; ~3,800 fled to Djibouti; 1,574 killed, 6,939 wounded since August (per UN figures via regional reporting). European Commission announced an additional EUR 22.5M Yemen aid on Oct 23 (2026 total EUR 110M).
sections.what_verified: OCHA/WFP are the primary sources of their own published figures (T1, official); the Geneva briefing is carried by UN News and multiple regional outlets. The 800,000 figure traces to WFP's Oct 14 statement, reaffirmed at the Oct 23 briefing.
sections.what_disputed: Siege attribution (Ansar Allah encirclement) is the UN agencies' characterisation; front lines around Taiz are contested and both sides restrict movement at various points — the briefing does not apportion every road closure. Casualty/displacement totals are UN estimates, not independently tallied here. Amnesty International has separately called for Taiz roads to reopen.
sections.why_matters: While missiles fly at Yanbu, 800,000 people in Taiz can't get food — water production halved, truck water tripled in price. The war's other front is hunger, and it has a UN count.
